recipes.name: Camarones al Ajillo (Garlic Shrimp)
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh large shrimp, shelled and deveined
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat the olive oil and butter in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the bell pepper and onion; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute more. Add the shrimp and cook until opaque, about 2 minutes on each side. Stir in the tomato sauce, parsley, and red pepper flakes, and cook until tomato sauce is warmed through, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Camarones al Ajillo (Garlic Shrimp)
raw_recipe.description: Large shrimp are cooked with ten cloves of garlic in this fragrant dish.

review.reviewBody: YUMM YUMMM YUMMM The only thing I did differently is that instead of the tomato sauce I used 1/4 cup of red cooking wine and 2 tbsp tomato paste (italian style from a tube)

Yum! I made this for my Puerto Rican girlfriend and she 100% approved! Just a few notes. First, tomato sauce is not the same thing as you'd put on spaghetti. It's actually more of a purée. Look for Goya tomato sauce in little cans. Also, I'm assuming "fresh" shrimp means uncooked. I couldn't find any uncooked shrimp on sale, so I added cooked shrimp, but not until the final 5 minutes when the tomato sauce went in. Any earlier than that and the shrimp will get mushy. 

I served over white rice, and if you want the full experience, make some plantain slices fried in olive oil as the side. There was a decent amount of leftovers even after 2 large plates each.
Just used the 1/4 cup cooking wine and 2 tbsp tube tomato paste instead of tomato sauce. It was fabulous. It will be on the menu a lot!

It's a really good start. I seasoned the shrimp while I was prepping the rest(sort of a dry cure), and like someone else here swapped the tomato sauce for a heaping tablespoon of tomato paste and sherry. Next time I plan to also add some carrot and celery, but it was good enough to merit a next time on it's own.

Delicious! I didn't have tomato sauce, so I followed another reviewer's suggestion and used 1/4 cup red wine and 2 tbsp tomato paste instead. I forgot the red pepper flakes and parsley, but it was still to die for.

I used a whole red pepper for this recipe. My garlic I minced. Also I used cooked shrimp, so I added them in at the same time as the tomato sauce so they didn't get over cooked. Other than that, left it as is and this dish was AMAZING!!!

This is a very good recipie! I tweaked it a little because my wife does not like tomato sauce, or spicy things. So in place of the sauce I just got a package of Lawrys Sundried tomato and garlic sauce, and Mixed that in. She also does not like spicy as well, so I cut out the peppers and put in paprika in place. But followed the rest of the recipie to a T. I Put it all on a bed of pasta,(would also go well with rice) and It came out with a VERY light Mediterranean taste. Definately season with salt and black pepper at the end, but it came out SO Flavorful! My wife said it was restraunt quality. I am rating this a 5 because this is a very EASY recipie with good results at the end.

Very simple, fast and delicious recipe. I didn't have the parsley so I used fresh chopped cilantro instead. I also added a small splash of pinot grigio white wine vinegar and it was a great touch. Easy recipe that when presented on a bed of white rice, looks like you spent a lot more time and effort making.

Delish! I generously wiped out the cast iron I had made bacon in this morning and used that (Like a boss!) :D Followed the recipe to the T (other than using fresh parsley) and it turned out amazing! Served over home-made yellow rice. Fantastic!
So very good! I made a few changes though. Doubled the green pepper, added one full cubed tomato, topped it with about an ounce of shredded goat cheese. Delicious!
Added Tony's creole seasoning and old bay with the recipe's seasonings before shrimp. Paired with mashed potatoes and crescent rolls.
This was so easy. The only change I made was using a few fresh tomatoes rather than sauce, so my husband would enjoy it more. As you season to your liking, it was just right. Served over rice.
Very good. Made with items that I always have. Simple, easy and delicious recipe. I served it over white rice with a side salad. Thank you for sharing.
Very tasty, easy to make, used fresh cilantro instead of the dry parsley, came out delicious, will definitely make it again
I have made this a few times now using the recipe as is except I used pre-cooked shrimp and a little extra red pepper flakes. I serve it with rice, very big hit at my house.
Made for the first time - loved this simple meal. I served it with spaghetti noodles and my husband loved it. Did not change anything
This was easy and tasted great. I made it with chicken...so good!

I made it exactly as written, i liked it, my mom loved it!!!
Husband doesn't eat shellfish, so no opinion from him.
